e.etymology: A clipped form of Bradley and Bradford, English surnames from place names: broad meadow and broad ford, with Old English brad, broad.
In birth records Infant is a placeholder written when a baby had not yet been named, so it shows up in name counts. The word comes from Latin infans, not yet speaking.
e.note: In US name data this is a records placeholder for unnamed newborns, not a name parents chose.

e.etymology: The Spanish word for solitude, shortened from María de la Soledad, Our Lady of Solitude, a title of the Virgin Mary honored on Good Friday.

e.meaning: brave ruler; pet form of Richard
e.etymology: A pet form of Richard, from Germanic ric, ruler, and hard, brave or hardy. It is also a Scottish surname from the same name.
namesakes: Ritchie Valens (1950s rock and roll singer of La Bamba)

e.etymology: From the Hawaiian word maile, a native vine with sweet-scented leaves that is woven into open lei for weddings, graduations and other honors.
From Sanskrit akasha, the sky or the open space of the heavens, one of the five elements in Indian philosophy.
A modern American blend of the Ja- beginning with Shawn, an Irish form of John.
A German and Austrian pet form of Elisabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, my God is an oath. Americans met it through the eldest von Trapp daughter in The Sound of Music.
namesakes: Liesl von Trapp (eldest daughter in The Sound of Music)

assoc.t: eldest von Trapp daughter in The Sound of Music

e.etymology: A respelling of Dallas, a Scottish surname taken from the village of Dallas in Moray and later the name of the Texas city.
As a girls' name, from Arabic saba, the soft easterly breeze of classical poetry. Saba is also the Arabic and Ethiopian name for the ancient kingdom of Sheba.
A respelling of Leona, the feminine form of Leo and Leon, from Latin leo, lion.
A respelling of Alana, the feminine form of Alan, a Celtic name of uncertain meaning that Breton settlers brought to Britain.
A Latin American spelling of Janet, a medieval pet form of Jane, which goes back through John to Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious.
From Hebrew ben, son, and Tsiyon, Zion: son of Zion. It is a traditional name in Jewish families, especially Orthodox ones.
A respelling of Harmony, the English word for agreement and musical concord, from Greek harmonia. The spelling echoes French harmonie, where the h is silent.
A modern spelling that overlaps with Jaya, a Sanskrit name meaning victory, and with the English short name Jay.
A modern combination of Lei and Anna, close to the older names Leanna and Liana.
A modern American coinage, a C- spelling of Kaleah, which joins the Ka- beginning with the sound of Leah.
A respelling of Fallon, from the Irish surname O Fallamhain, descendant of Fallamhan, a personal name meaning leader.
The Ethiopian and Eritrean form of Hripsime (Rhipsime), a 4th-century martyr of Armenia who is a much-loved saint in the Ethiopian Orthodox Church.
From Old Irish Finn, a byname from find: white, bright, fair. It is the name of Fionn mac Cumhaill, the hunter-warrior hero of Irish legend, and the original of Finn.
namesakes: Fionn mac Cumhaill (hero of Irish legend)
e.note: Americans often read it as fee-ON; in Ireland it is said like Finn or with a soft y, FYUN.

e.etymology: An English surname from Middle English seely, happy or blessed, the same word that later turned into silly.
namesakes: Seeley Booth (FBI agent on the TV series Bones)

assoc.t: Seeley Booth, the FBI agent of the TV series Bones

e.etymology: The West African form of Khadija, used in Guinea, Mali and Senegal. Khadija, the first wife of the Prophet Muhammad, bore an Arabic name usually explained as early-born child.
A spelling of Viraj, from Sanskrit viraj, shining out or ruling far and wide; in Hindu texts Viraj is a name for the primeval being.
The Scottish Gaelic form of Alexander, from Greek alexo, to defend, and aner, man. Alistair and Alastair are its anglicized spellings.
A modern American name built on Xavier with the -ion ending of names like Davion and Javion; this spelling writes out the long a.
The Danish form of Old Norse Thorbjorn, from Thor, the thunder god, and bjorn, bear.
A respelling of Isaiah, from Hebrew Yeshayahu, the Lord is salvation, the name of the Old Testament prophet.
A respelling of Azalea, the flowering shrub, whose name comes from Greek azaleos, dry, for the dry soil it was thought to like.
An Arabic name usually explained as strong or firm. It honors al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, a close companion of the Prophet Muhammad.
The English adjective steely, hard and strong as steel, and also an English surname. Its use as a girls' name is very recent.
